candidates.exact_span: The permittee shall operate an industrial pretreatment program in accordance with Section 402(b)(8) of the Clean Water Act, the General Pretreatment Regulations (40 CFR Part 403) and the approved POTW pretreatment program submitted by the permittee.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This clause ties enforceable obligations to externally incorporated authorities (CWA section, 40 CFR Part 403, and an approved program not reproduced in the segment). Different readings of which incorporated provisions apply in Federal FY2025 would change which numeric pretreatment standards count as enforceable limits (A), which monitoring duties are in force (B), and how missing or conditional evidence should be classified when applicability depends on off-segment program text (C).

candidates.exact_span: The POTW pretreatment program is hereby incorporated by reference and shall be implemented in a manner consistent with the following requirements:
candidates.computation_change_reason: Incorporation by reference makes obligations depend on the content of the separately submitted/approved pretreatment program. If that referenced document is read narrowly or broadly, the set of FY2025 monitoring requirements deemed applicable (B) and whether absent results reflect conditional non-requirement versus unresolved missing evidence (C) can change.

candidates.exact_span: Industrial user information shall be updated at a frequency adequate to ensure that all IUs are properly characterized at all times;
candidates.computation_change_reason: The required update frequency is not numerically fixed and hinges on interpretation of "adequate" and "properly characterized." That affects whether an information-maintenance obligation was actually applicable during specific FY2025 periods (B) and whether gaps in characterization evidence are documented non-requirement, other no-data, or unresolved (C).

candidates.exact_span: The frequency and nature of industrial user compliance monitoring activities by the permittee shall be commensurate with the character, consistency and volume of waste.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Monitoring frequency and type are conditioned on waste character, consistency, and volume without fixed schedules in this span. Different interpretations of those qualifiers would change which permittee monitoring activities were required in FY2025 (B) and whether periods without samples reflect conditional non-requirement versus inadequate evidence (C).

candidates.exact_span: The permittee must inspect and sample the effluent from each Significant Industrial User in accordance with 40 CFR 403.8(f)(2)(v).
candidates.computation_change_reason: This establishes a mandatory inspection and sampling duty for each Significant Industrial User, but both SIU status and the operative details of 40 CFR 403.8(f)(2)(v) are external to the segment. Resolving those dependencies differently changes which FY2025 monitoring was required (B) and how to treat missing effluent results for SIUs (C).

candidates.exact_span: This is in addition to any industrial self-monitoring activities
candidates.computation_change_reason: The phrase allocates monitoring responsibility between permittee sampling and industrial-user self-monitoring. Interpreting whether a given parameter or period is satisfied by self-monitoring alone, or still requires permittee inspection/sampling, changes evaluated monitoring obligations (B) and whether missing permittee data is excused or remains an evidence gap (C).

candidates.exact_span: The permittee shall control through permit, order, or similar means, the contribution to the POTW by each Industrial User to ensure compliance with applicable Pretreatment Standards and Requirements.
candidates.computation_change_reason: "Applicable Pretreatment Standards and Requirements" are not enumerated here, and control mechanisms (permit, order, or similar) may themselves impose numeric limits and monitoring schedules. Different readings of which standards attach to which industrial users would change enforceable limit selection (A) and derived monitoring duties (B).

candidates.exact_span: In the case of Industrial Users identified as significant under 40 CFR 403.3(v), this control shall be achieved through individual or general control mechanisms, in accordance with
candidates.computation_change_reason: Significance under 40 CFR 403.3(v) is a classification threshold that triggers stricter control mechanisms and interacts with the SIU sampling duty elsewhere in this segment. Who qualifies as significant, and which incorporated control mechanism applies, affects which numeric pretreatment limits bind (A), which monitoring is required (B), and how to classify missing results for users near the significance threshold (C). The locator text is truncated in the source segment, adding locator-boundary uncertainty.
